topic: Falls risk screening and multifactorial assessment

audits.title: 196 A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE TO OPTIMISE PHYSIOTHERAPY FALLS ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION
audits.standard: Every patient referred to physiotherapy aged over 65 or at risk of falls receives a personalised falls assessment and intervention
audits.setting: Physiotherapy department, St James's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Falls assessment 57%; fear of falling assessment 30%; falls outcome measures 26%; falls intervention 49%.

audits.intervention: Physiotherapy falls committee, 'Ask, Assess, Intervene' falls algorithm, in-service and induction training, falls champions, weekly falls newsletter, updated electronic physiotherapy assessment forms, and a falls prevention booklet and online education talk.

cycle2.result: Falls assessment 99%; fear of falling assessment 88%; falls outcome measures 74%; falls intervention 100%.

audits.other_findings: Gait and balance deficits were assessed in 94% at the final audit; audits ran weekly then monthly.
audits.citation: Mealy B, Keohane N. 196 A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT INITIATIVE TO OPTIMISE PHYSIOTHERAPY FALLS ASSESSMENT AND INTERVENTION. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_3):ii9-ii41. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab219.196.

audits.title: 21 An audit of vision assessment in patients presenting for a review of falls
audits.standard: NICE 2013 falls guideline (formal vision assessment for all) and BGS/RCP bedside vision assessment tool
audits.setting: Geriatric service, St Vincent's University Hospital (Caritas), Dublin

cycle1.result: 11 (69%) not asked about vision; of 5 asked, only 2 had documented visual field assessment; none had all RCP-recommended checks.

audits.intervention: Planned: basic visual assessment tools (e.g. Snellen chart), updated falls proforma and staff education before re-audit.
audits.other_findings: 7 (44.7%) had visual problems or conditions affecting vision.
audits.citation: Noonan B, Cosgrave S, Nunes F, Cooney M. 21 An audit of vision assessment in patients presenting for a review of falls. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.002.

audits.title: An Audit Of Fall Risk Screening, Using The 3 Key Questions, In Physiotherapy Initial Assessment Documentation In Primary Care
audits.standard: World Guidelines for Falls Prevention 2022: all adults ≥65 asked the 3 Key Questions, with assessment and referral if any answer is yes
audits.setting: Physiotherapy initial assessments across 6 Primary Care teams, HSE Galway

cycle1.result: Compliance 70% for Question 1, 36.7% for Question 2 and 23.3% for Question 3; 66.7% documented follow-up actions based on responses.

audits.intervention: 3KQ added to physiotherapy assessment forms, risk stratification algorithm displayed in treatment rooms and staff guidance on referral.
audits.citation: Hayes A, Tierney E, McMahon S, O'Keeffe L, Curtayne L, Lydon M, et al.. An Audit Of Fall Risk Screening, Using The 3 Key Questions, In Physiotherapy Initial Assessment Documentation In Primary Care. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.060.

audits.title: 289 Detection of Falls in Older Patients by Medical Professionals on Admission to Hospital: An Audit
audits.standard: HSE best practice guidelines: all patients over 65 asked whether they have fallen in the past year, with frequency, context and characteristics
audits.setting: Emergency medical admissions, acute hospital (Our Lady's Hospital, Navan)

cycle1.result: Only 3 (25%) patients were screened for falls at admission.

audits.intervention: New admission proforma containing a falls screening questionnaire, with an information session on its use.

cycle2.result: 58% of admissions screened for falls; 40% of those screened had fallen in the last year.

audits.other_findings: Of falls identified in the re-audit, 75% were mechanical and 25% due to other causes.
audits.citation: Buckley E, Alalawi M. 289 Detection of Falls in Older Patients by Medical Professionals on Admission to Hospital: An Audit. Age and Ageing. 2019;48(Supplement_3):iii17-iii65. doi:10.1093/ageing/afz103.183.

audits.title: Preventing falls in older people: charting practice change by audit.
audits.standard: Formal falls risk assessment for older patients
audits.setting: Elderly Mental Health Services, North Dorset Primary Care NHS Trust

cycle1.result: There was no formal means of assessing falls risk before the audit.

audits.intervention: Staff awareness raised and a specific falls-risk assessment developed.

cycle2.result: Follow-up audits showed a change in practice, with the assessment widely used (numbers not reported).

audits.citation: Mitchell E, Dyer J. Preventing falls in older people: charting practice change by audit. Prof Nurse. 2002;17(11):665-668. PMID: 12138583.

audits.title: Management of older patients presenting after a fall--an accident and emergency department audit.
audits.standard: Assessment and correction of fall risk factors (no specific guideline stated)
audits.setting: Accident and emergency department, Groote Schuur Hospital, Cape Town

cycle1.result: Previous falls and drug or alcohol history recorded in under 20%; postural blood pressure 2%; cognitive assessment under 30%; no referrals to geriatric medicine, physiotherapy or occupational therapy.

audits.other_findings: Blood pressure and pulse recorded in about 90%, radiology in 89%; 52% referred to orthopaedic surgery.
audits.citation: Kalula SZ, de Villiers L, Ross K, Ferreira M. Management of older patients presenting after a fall--an accident and emergency department audit. S Afr Med J. 2006;96(8):718-721. PMID: 17019495.

audits.title: Emergency department management of falls in the elderly: A clinical audit and suggestions for improvement.
audits.standard: Institutionally approved optimum care for falls in patients aged 60 and over
audits.setting: Emergency department, Emam Hossein Hospital, Tehran

cycle1.result: Most common omissions: Romberg test not done (92.75%) and no physiotherapy consultation (82.75%)

audits.intervention: Educational programme based on Delphi expert panel suggestions

cycle2.result: Educational programme had a modest effect on improving care (beta = 3.79)

audits.other_findings: Wide gap between delivered care and international standards.
audits.citation: Hatamabadi HR, Hatamabadi HR, Sum S, Tabatabaey A, Sabbaghi M. Emergency department management of falls in the elderly: A clinical audit and suggestions for improvement. Int Emerg Nurs. 2016;24:2-8. doi:10.1016/j.ienj.2015.05.001. PMID: 26048537.

audits.title: Falls Risk Assessment Compliance and Outcomes in Psychiatry of Old Age Inpatient Department
audits.standard: NICE CG161: falls risk assessment within 24 hours of admission with interventions for identified risks
audits.setting: 8-bed Psychiatry of Old Age inpatient unit, Dublin

cycle1.result: 4 of 5 patients (80%) assessed within 24 hours with risks addressed within 48 hours; clinical documentation present for all (100%); 4 falls recorded, all documented (100%)

audits.intervention: Education for team members on timely and accurate falls risk assessment
audits.other_findings: Cycle one was judged compliant, but documentation quality and consistency needed improvement. Cycle 2 data collection was under way.
audits.citation: Khan H, Butler A. Falls Risk Assessment Compliance and Outcomes in Psychiatry of Old Age Inpatient Department. BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S312-S313.
